provenance: Original synthetic examples authored for this demonstration; not derived from third-party datasets.
label_criteria: Within each group, preference reflects the stated requirement as judged during example construction; labels are not derived from training feature values and are not real-world reliability outcomes.

groups.requirement: Parse an integer without executing arbitrary input.

candidates.reason: Converts a number without evaluating code.

groups.requirement: Pass a filename as an argument without shell interpretation.

candidates.reason: Uses an argument list without a shell.
Still lets the shell interpret the filename.

groups.requirement: Read a secret from the environment instead of embedding it in source.

candidates.reason: Configuration comes from outside the source.
The value remains embedded in source.

groups.requirement: Derive a password key with a salt and PBKDF2 instead of a plain fast hash.

candidates.reason: Uses salted password key derivation; salt management still requires review.

groups.requirement: Create a temporary file using an API that creates it securely.

candidates.reason: Creates the temporary file rather than returning an unchecked name.

groups.requirement: Catch only invalid integer input rather than hiding every exception.

candidates.reason: Limits the handler to invalid input.

groups.requirement: Parse a Python literal without evaluating arbitrary code.

candidates.reason: Parses literals without evaluating arbitrary expressions.

groups.requirement: Preserve a syntactically valid function that returns the input.

candidates.reason: The function remains syntactically valid and meets the stated requirement.
The incomplete replacement is not syntactically valid.
